facts.text: On this date in 1944, Paris was liberated after four years of Nazi occupation — yet the city suffered almost no structural damage, partly because the German commander Dietrich von Choltitz defied Hitler's direct order to burn it to the ground.
On this date in 1916, the U.S. National Park Service was founded — it now manages 85 million acres across 63 parks, more land than the entire country of Germany.
More people live inside a 40-mile radius of Jakarta than in all of Australia. The Indonesian capital's metro area holds roughly 35 million people on a landmass smaller than Connecticut.
Canada has more lakes than every other country on Earth combined — over 60% of the world's total. Much of that water sits in landscape scoured by glaciers less than 12,000 years ago.
Lesotho, San Marino, and Uzbekistan are the only countries in the world entirely surrounded by just one other country — a geographic quirk that makes each one a nation-within-a-nation.
On this day in 1921, the Dow Jones fell 7% in a single session as post-WWI deflation peaked — then began a decade-long bull run that would multiply it sixfold by 1929.
On this day in 1987, the Dow hit what was then an all-time high of 2,722. Eight weeks later, Black Monday erased 22% of that in a single afternoon.
The S&P 500 has spent roughly 75% of all trading days below its all-time high — meaning patient waiting, not bold timing, defines most of investing's actual texture.
At its 1999 peak, Cisco was briefly the most valuable company on Earth at $555 billion. It has never returned to that price per share, 26 years later.
The Dutch East India Company, adjusted for inflation, had a peak market cap of roughly $8 trillion — larger than today's Apple, Microsoft, and Nvidia combined.
On this day in 1989, Voyager 2 passed Neptune — the only spacecraft ever to do so. It remains the most distant human-made object to have completed a planetary encounter.
On this day in 1835, the Great Moon Hoax began: the New York Sun published six articles describing bat-winged humanoids on the Moon, briefly becoming the world's best-selling newspaper.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere roughly the size of a city. A teaspoon of its material would weigh about a billion tons on Earth.
Your skeleton is not static. Nearly every bone in your body is completely replaced, cell by cell, approximately every decade — you are not carrying the bones you were born with.
Quantum entanglement has been demonstrated across distances exceeding 1,200 kilometers. Two particles can share a state instantaneously, yet this still cannot transmit information faster than light.
On this day in 1609, Galileo demonstrated his telescope to Venetian senators — who immediately used it to spot enemy ships. The universe could wait; the navy could not.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. Ancient Egypt was already ancient history to her.
On this day in 1916, the U.S. National Park Service was founded — meaning the agency protecting Yellowstone is younger than the Eiffel Tower.
Oxford University was teaching students before the Aztec Empire existed. It held lectures for a century before Tenochtitlan broke ground.
The fax machine was patented in 1843 — before the American Civil War, before the telephone, before anyone had seen a photograph taken outdoors.
Meraki (μεράκι): Greek for doing something with soul, creativity, or love — leaving a piece of yourself in your work. There is no English equivalent, which says something about English.
Sonder: the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined in 2012 by John Koenig; too useful to stay obscure.
On this day in 1609, Galileo demonstrated his telescope to Venetian senators. The Italian word for telescope — 'cannocchiale' — means 'hollow reed for the eye.' The poetry was there from the start.
Hiraeth (Welsh): a homesickness for a home you cannot return to, or never had. It folds grief, longing, and belonging into a single syllable cluster no other language has matched.
On this day in 1944, Paris was liberated. French gave us 'dépaysement' — the disorienting, bittersweet feeling of being in a foreign place. That August, Paris felt it in reverse.

On this date in 2012, Coinbase officially launched to the public — a YC-backed startup that let Americans buy Bitcoin via bank transfer. It would become the first crypto exchange listed on a US stock exchange, nine years later.
On Aug 25, 2021, Ethereum's EIP-1559 had been live for two weeks, having already burned over 50,000 ETH — permanently removing it from supply through ordinary transaction fees.

Bitcoin's smallest unit, the satoshi, is 0.00000001 BTC. At Bitcoin's current scale, the entire global supply of 2.1 quadrillion satoshis fits in a 64-bit integer — a deliberate engineering choice by Satoshi.

The DAO hack of 2016 didn't exploit Ethereum's consensus layer. It exploited a reentrancy bug in Solidity smart contract code — the chain itself worked exactly as designed, which is why the fix required a hard fork.

Satoshi Nakamoto's known wallet addresses have never moved a single satoshi since 2010. On-chain, this inactivity is itself verifiable — and makes those coins a permanent, auditable ghost in Bitcoin's ledger.
On this date in 2012, Alex Krizhevsky submitted AlexNet to ImageNet. Its 10.8-point error gap over second place was so large that organizers initially assumed a scoring error.
Today in 2016, DeepMind's WaveNet paper dropped — a raw audio model so computationally expensive it took 90 minutes of GPU time to generate one second of speech.
GPT-4's training run is estimated to have consumed roughly 50 GWh of electricity — comparable to the annual power draw of 4,500 average American homes.
The transformer architecture, now foundational to nearly every major AI system, was introduced in 2017 by a team of eight authors, six of whom have since left Google.
Chinchilla scaling laws showed in 2022 that most large language models were dramatically undertrained — GPT-3's optimal dataset size was roughly 20x larger than what OpenAI used.
